name: regexpu-core-unicodeflag-option-now-opt-in-buble
behavioral_change: regexpu-core v5.0.0 changed `rewritePattern` so that each rewriting feature must be explicitly enabled. In v_old (4.5.4), any `u` flag caused ES2015 unicode patterns to be rewritten to ES5 unconditionally; in v_new (5.3.2) this is governed by the `unicodeFlag` option (false or 'transform'), whose default false leaves the pattern untouched, so `rewritePattern('foo.bar', 'u')` now returns `foo.bar` unchanged.
downstream_effect: The downstream compiler buble calls `rewritePattern(pattern, flags)` in src/program/types/Literal.js and strips the `u` flag from its output, so after the upgrade `/foo.bar/u` is compiled to `/foo.bar/` with silently changed semantics. The single failure is an AssertionError comparing compiled output to the expected sample, with frames only in test/test.js; Literal.js, rewritePattern, regexpu-core and unicodeFlag never appear, although the test title "transpiles regex with unicode flag" names the affected feature.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in src/program/types/Literal.js:33 from `rewritePattern(pattern, flags)` to `rewritePattern(pattern, flags, { unicodeFlag: 'transform' })`.
documented_in: The regexpu-core 5.x README (https://github.com/mathiasbynens/regexpu-core/blob/v5.0.0/README.md), section "Stable regular expression features", describes the `unicodeFlag` option with the example `rewritePattern('\u{ab}', 'u', { unicodeFlag: 'transform' })`; there is no CHANGELOG or release note for 5.0.0 announcing the change, and the same README still shows the old behavior in several examples.
failing_tests: test/test.js :: buble > regex.js > transpiles regex with unicode flag
